sources.fact: 2021 Help shows a second concentric mate overdefining an assembly if the two hole-centre distances differ.
2021 Help recommends MateXpert, examining red mates, suppressing conflicting mates, DOF inspection and considering fixed components.
2021 Help describes deliberately allowed concentric misalignment with an option/tolerance and separate Misaligned mate folder.

symptoms: Adding a second concentric mate produces an over-defined assembly.
A formerly solved concentric mate conflicts after geometry or fixed-state changes.
Two mating hole patterns are nearly aligned but exact concentric constraints cannot both be solved.
rivals: Hole-to-hole centre distances differ between two components, making exact coaxiality impossible for both pairs.
Other mates restrict a component position or degrees of freedom and conflict with the requested axis.
A component is fixed or an in-context reference changed, preventing desired alignment.
Intended design permits finite misalignment, but exact concentric relations were incorrectly specified.

probes.test: On a disposable assembly copy, inspect the two hole axes and compare centre-to-centre spacings of the paired holes in the respective part coordinate contexts, before adding an exact second concentric mate.
probes.conditions: 2021 assembly, active configuration and component transforms; lengths in mm; record each pair, measurement method and applied mates; read-only geometry inspection on a copy.
probes.rivals: Mismatched hole spacing versus conflict solely from another mate.
probes.basis: DOCUMENTED: Example: Concentric Mate Error; measurement-based diagnosis is a hypothesis.
probes.member: not applicable: UI-only procedure; no API member asserted

outcomes.observation: Corresponding hole spacings differ beyond measurement tolerance
outcomes.meaning: Explains why two exact concentric mates cannot generally be satisfied simultaneously.
outcomes.limits: Does not prove the mismatch is an unintended CAD error or rule out additional mate conflicts.
outcomes.next_step: Confirm engineering design intent, hole tolerances and optional misalignment capability.

outcomes.observation: Hole spacings agree within measured resolution but mate fails
outcomes.meaning: Weakens pitch mismatch as sole explanation.
outcomes.limits: Axes may be angled or another mate/fixed state may still conflict.
outcomes.next_step: Inspect MateXpert and existing degrees of freedom.

outcomes.observation: Inconclusive: axes/centres or configurations are not comparable
outcomes.limits: Do not treat approximate graphics alignment as exact geometry.
outcomes.next_step: Identify comparable axial geometry and consistent coordinate frame.

probes.test: In a disposable copy, run MateXpert/View Mate Errors, inspect highlighted red mates and component fixed states; temporarily suppress one competing mate at a time and inspect remaining degrees of freedom.
probes.conditions: Record assembly/configuration, pre-existing mate graph and suppression changes; suppressing or floating changes assembly state; only disposable fixture; avoid Force Mate because it can break other mates.
probes.rivals: Conflicting mate network / fixed component versus intrinsically impossible geometric relationship.
probes.basis: DOCUMENTED: Techniques for Fixing Mate Problems; resolving a mate after suppression is conditional evidence.
probes.member: not applicable: UI-only procedure; no API member asserted

outcomes.observation: Target concentric mate solves only when another mate is suppressed or a component floated
outcomes.meaning: The suppressed mate/fixed condition participates in the conflict.
outcomes.limits: Does not mean suppressing it is the correct design solution.
outcomes.next_step: Review desired kinematic degrees of freedom and replace a redundant constraint deliberately.

outcomes.observation: Target mate still fails after irrelevant mates are suppressed
outcomes.meaning: The tested conflicts were not sufficient to explain failure.
outcomes.limits: A geometry mismatch, remaining constraint or stale reference may still exist.
outcomes.next_step: Compare hole axes/pitches and inspect mate references.

outcomes.observation: Inconclusive: MateXpert cannot identify sources or suppression yields unstable results
outcomes.meaning: No reliable unique conflicting mate identified.
outcomes.limits: Do not use Force Mate to claim causal isolation.
outcomes.next_step: Construct minimal two-component test assembly from copies.

probes.test: If design permits intentional mismatch, inspect the misaligned-concentric-mate option and tolerance on disposable assembly; compare exact-mate failure with explicitly permitted misalignment.
probes.conditions: 2021 assembly, recorded linear misalignment tolerance in mm, actual hole spacing difference and position; enabling this changes mate conditions, so disposable copy only.
probes.rivals: Design-approved misalignment versus accidental geometric overdefinition.
probes.basis: DOCUMENTED: Allowing Misaligned Concentric Mates; correctness for a particular design requires separate engineering judgement.
probes.member: not applicable: UI-only procedure; no API member asserted

outcomes.observation: Second mate succeeds only with nonzero allowed misalignment
outcomes.meaning: Supports deliberate mismatch accommodation as the mechanism.
outcomes.limits: Does not establish acceptable fit, stress, assembly or manufacturing tolerance.
outcomes.next_step: Check tolerancing and functional design intent before accepting any model change.

outcomes.observation: Second mate still fails with allowed misalignment
outcomes.meaning: Specified tolerance or another conflict may be insufficient.
outcomes.limits: Does not disprove mismatch as a contributor.
outcomes.next_step: Compare the residual error to allowed tolerance and inspect other mates.

outcomes.observation: Inconclusive: option unavailable or permission/design tolerance unknown
outcomes.meaning: No conclusion about whether misalignment is intended.
outcomes.limits: Do not silently add tolerance to make the assembly solve.
outcomes.next_step: Record unmet option or engineering design clarification as unresolved.

limitations: A solvable mate does not prove dimensional fit or mechanical correctness.
Enabling misalignment changes assembly constraint semantics; must not be presented as generic repair.
No installed SOLIDWORKS runtime tests, actual assemblies or API calls were performed.
